transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're eager to get back to gardening! According to our guidelines, you can start with light exercise, like gardening, about 1 week after surgery. Just remember to take it easy and avoid any heavy lifting or bending. Also, be careful not to get any water in your eyes. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you! Next, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using the preservative-free eye drops we recommended as soon as you need to. In fact, it's a good idea to start using them four times a day to help with any dryness or discomfort. You can get more from your GP if you need to. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, thank you. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's common to feel like your eyes are more sensitive to light after cataract surgery. If it's just a bit of discomfort and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help. But if you're experiencing significant pain or if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to check it further. Would you like to ask another question?
